terms.comment: festīnāre tē nōlō is Cicero’s (Fam. 16.11.1). Augustus’ “make haste slowly” was Greek, σπεῦδε βραδέως (Suet. Aug. 25; Gell. 10.11.5); festīnā lentē is the later Latin form.

phrases.english: Slowly! I don’t want you to rush.

phrases.latin: Nōlī tantum cibī simul in ōs inserere! Lentius mandūcā!
phrases.english: Don’t put so much food in your mouth at once! Chew more slowly!

sources: Cicero and the Augustus note from the Latinitas loci collections.
